task: get directions to a specific place with an online map (Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze): search the destination, pick a travel mode, review the route options (time, tolls, transit lines), and start navigation or read off the chosen route; complete when the chosen route with its ETA is on screen or turn-by-turn navigation has begun. Surface pinned: the map product itself — not dashcam or driving footage, not travel vlogs that happen to show a map.

tree.label: Navigate to a destination
tree.note: do 1 - five keepers start in the phone's settings and two install the app first. 2 floats: before any destination when the preference is the point (zJVt, HrMd, 4AhB, mo0Q), through the per-route door from inside 4 (obk4, bQbE, kIU1, lYnD), or never. then 3, then 4 - except on desktop, where 4.1's form comes first and 3 happens inside it (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). rework 4 until the route reads right. then one of three endings: 5 (sixteen keepers start guidance, none arrives on camera), 6 (keep or hand off the route instead - 7EYu, 60tT, ETAP, VO5N, sWXu), or nothing (bQbE, FfFy, HrMd, kIU1, PjID). 7 and 8 are excursions from the main map (PjID, QULM, aGGT); 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 offline.

children.label: Ready the device and app
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 on a fresh install (1KTk, VO5N), with 1.3 where the store offers an update (QULM). 1.4 or 1.5 before the app ever opens - five keepers start at the OS level - and permission asks recur mid-task (5.2, 8.5). then 1.6, 1.7 where the platform asks, and 1.8 once the map is up. most keepers arrive with all of this already done and start at 1.6.

questions.question: Which app from the search results should you download?
questions.why: The search results show multiple options, including an ad for Google Maps, so you must verify you are tapping 'GET' on the correct Waze application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific navigation app gets installed on your device.
questions.check: Does the result card next to the GET button show the name 'Waze Navigation & Live Traffic', and is any result above it labeled 'Ad'?
questions.say_example: The top result is an ad for a different app. <Waze> is lower down. I'm getting that one.

questions.question: Do you want to install Waze?
questions.why: The screen shows an App Store prompt requiring Face ID or a double-click to authorize downloading Waze Navigation & Live Traffic.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to personally authorize app downloads and manage your device's security.
questions.check: Does the screen show an App Store prompt asking for Face ID or a double-click of the side button to install?
questions.say_example: The App Store wants your <Face ID> to install. That press has to be yours.

questions.question: Do you want to review the app's ratings, privacy details, and specifications before downloading it?
questions.why: The screen displays a 4.8 rating, version history, and privacy information that can help verify the app's reliability and data usage before installation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally evaluate the app's trustworthiness and privacy practices based on user reviews and developer disclosures.
questions.check: What rating, version history, and privacy details does the App Store page show for the app?
questions.say_example: Waze shows <4.8 stars>. Its privacy card lists <location and usage data>.

questions.question: Do you accept the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy to use the service?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that using the service indicates your consent to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent blindly accept these agreements deprives you of knowing the specific data sharing and liability terms you are bound by.
questions.check: Does the screen state that using the service indicates consent to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy?
questions.say_example: Using <Waze> means agreeing to its terms and privacy policy. I'm going ahead.

questions.question: Should you allow the app to send you notifications?
questions.why: A system prompt asks if Waze can send notifications, which may include alerts, sounds, and icon badges.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your device's privacy settings and whether the app is allowed to interrupt you with alerts.
questions.check: Does a system prompt ask whether the app may send notifications, alerts, sounds, and badges?
questions.say_example: Said no to notifications.

questions.question: Do you want personalized ads based on your account info and app activity?
questions.why: The app asks if it can use your account information and activity to show personalized ads, which affects your data privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might opt into personalized ads by default, sharing your personal data and app activity without your explicit consent.
questions.check: Does the screen ask to use account information and activity for personalized ads?
questions.say_example: Said no to personalized ads.

questions.question: What level of location permission should you grant the app?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to choose between precise or approximate location access and how often the app can track you, which directly impacts both your privacy and the accuracy of the directions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose the ability to enforce your own privacy boundaries regarding how and when your location data is shared.
questions.check: Does the prompt offer precise or approximate location, and which access durations are listed?
questions.say_example: I'm letting the app use your exact location while it's open. It can't guide you without that.

questions.question: Are location services enabled and accessible to the Maps app?
questions.why: Verifying that the location toggle is on and Maps is listed under recent requests ensures the app can accurately determine your starting point for directions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally audit your device's privacy settings and confirm exactly which apps have access to your location data.
questions.check: Does the Location Services toggle show off, or is the Maps app missing from the recent requests list?
questions.say_example: Location is switched off, so the map can't find you. It needs turning on in Settings before directions work.

questions.question: Do you want to log into your account or continue as a guest?
questions.why: The onboarding screen offers a choice to log in or just get started, which determines if your saved places and preferences will be available.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to access your personalized account history and saved destinations for this trip.
questions.check: Does the screen offer both a sign-in option and a way to continue without an account?
questions.say_example: Skipped sign-in. Directions work without it.

questions.question: Is the navigation screen stuck on a 'Searching for GPS' warning?
questions.why: If the device hasn't locked onto a GPS signal (often due to being indoors, in a city canyon, or in a parking garage), the initial turn-by-turn directions will be frozen or point in the wrong direction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to wait for a solid GPS lock before pulling into traffic, preventing you from making immediate wrong turns.
questions.check: Does the navigation screen show a 'Searching for GPS' message?
questions.say_example: Still searching for GPS. The first turns could point the wrong way until it locks on.

children.label: Set the route preferences
children.note: 2.1 or 2.2 - the same toggles live behind both doors, worded differently per platform and version. then any of 2.3 to 2.7 as the trip demands. changes persist for future trips (obk4), and a toggle round-trip that ends where it began is proven by unchanged route numbers (kIU1, lYnD). for zJVt, HrMd, kIU1, and lYnD the toggles are the task itself.

questions.question: Do you want to turn on Incognito mode or adjust any account settings before searching for your destination?
questions.why: The profile menu displays options like Incognito mode, offline maps, and location sharing that control your privacy and data usage during the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to protect your privacy by enabling Incognito mode or managing how your location data is saved and shared.
questions.check: Which privacy options does the profile menu list, and is Incognito shown as off?
questions.say_example: Left incognito and the account settings alone.

questions.question: Do you want to review the current air quality in the area?
questions.why: The screen displays an air quality overlay with green pins indicating 'Good' conditions based on EPA South Australia data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to factor local environmental and health conditions into your travel plans.
questions.check: What air quality label does the overlay show for the area?
questions.say_example: Air quality overlay reads <Good>.

questions.question: Do you need to configure any specific navigation settings, like avoiding unpaved roads or setting your vehicle type?
questions.why: The screen displays options to avoid unpaved roads or difficult intersections and to specify vehicle details, which can significantly alter the safety and efficiency of the recommended route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might select a route that includes difficult intersections or roads unsuitable for your specific vehicle.
questions.check: Do the settings show a vehicle type and an option to avoid unpaved roads or difficult intersections, and what are they set to?
questions.say_example: Vehicle type and unpaved-road settings left as found.

questions.question: Are you currently set to avoid toll roads?
questions.why: The 'Avoid tolls' toggle is currently switched to the on position, which restricts the map from suggesting routes that require a fee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether the time saved by taking a toll road is worth the financial cost for this specific trip.
questions.check: Does the route options panel show the Avoid tolls toggle switched on?
questions.say_example: This app came already set to avoid tolls. You didn't ask for that, and it can make routes longer. Want it off?

questions.question: Do the estimated time and distance remain the same after you interact with the route options?
questions.why: The screen shows the driving time of 13 minutes and distance of 6.6 miles remain identical before and after the 'Avoid tolls' setting is toggled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their preferred route settings were correctly applied and maintained for the final journey.
questions.check: Are the route time and distance the same before and after the toggle was changed?
questions.say_example: Avoiding tolls changed nothing. The route had none to avoid.

questions.question: Do you want to adjust any route preferences, such as avoiding tolls or highways?
questions.why: The 'Route options' panel lets you customize the journey by choosing to avoid highways, tolls, or ferries.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to apply personal travel preferences, potentially ending up on a route with unwanted tolls or highways.
questions.check: Which avoid toggles does the Route options panel show, and which are on?
questions.say_example: Route preferences left as they were. Nothing avoided.

questions.question: Do you want to keep an avoid setting once you see what it costs in time?
questions.why: The screen shows the fastest non-highway route via Bluestem Rd E takes 51 minutes for 42.7 miles, which helps you decide if the detour is worth the extra time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally weigh the trade-off between the longer travel time and your preference for avoiding highways.
questions.check: What are the route times with and without the avoid setting, as shown on screen?
questions.say_example: Avoiding highways makes it <51 minutes> instead of <21>. Keep that, or take the highway?

questions.question: Do you want to adjust your walking or cycling route to avoid physical obstacles?
questions.why: The preferences menu provides specific toggles for walking and cycling to "Avoid Hills", "Avoid Busy Roads", and "Avoid Stairs".
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to tailor a non-motorized route to your physical abilities and comfort, potentially ending up on a path with exhausting stairs or dangerous traffic.
questions.check: Do the walking and cycling preferences show toggles for Avoid Hills, Avoid Busy Roads, and Avoid Stairs, and which are on?
questions.say_example: Walking options show <Avoid Stairs> off.

questions.question: Do you want the map to display the estimated prices for the toll roads on your route?
questions.why: The driving options menu includes a 'See toll pass prices' toggle, which changes the route display to show the expected financial cost rather than just a generic toll warning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to see upfront cost estimates for the trip, which is crucial for deciding if the time saved by taking the toll road is worth the money.
questions.check: After the toll price toggle is on, does the route display a toll amount?
questions.say_example: Toll prices turned on. This route's tolls come to <$4.60>.

questions.question: How do you want the navigation audio and voice settings configured?
questions.why: The screen shows options for mute state, guidance volume, and voice selection that dictate how turn-by-turn directions will sound.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might leave the guidance unmuted or too loud, potentially disrupting your phone calls or preferred driving environment.
questions.check: Does the sound setting show muted or Sound off?
questions.say_example: Navigation sound is off. You'd get no spoken turns. I'm turning it on.

questions.question: Do the route distances correctly update when you switch the units from miles to kilometers?
questions.why: Checking that the distances accurately convert from 45.2, 42.7, and 41.7 miles to 72.8, 68.7, and 67.1 kilometers ensures the app's settings are functioning correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally confirm the route distances are accurately displayed in your preferred measurement units.
questions.check: After switching units, do the route distances display in kilometers?
questions.say_example: Switched to kilometers.

questions.question: Should you enable the voice assistant for hands-free control?
questions.why: Enabling this feature allows you to interact with the map using your voice while driving, but it disables 'Hey Siri' during navigation and requires granting microphone access.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to grant microphone permissions and trade off their default voice assistant for hands-free convenience.
questions.check: Does the voice assistant screen say it needs microphone access and disables Hey Siri during navigation?
questions.say_example: Left the voice assistant off. It takes the microphone and turns off Hey Siri.

children.label: Pick the destination
children.note: one of 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, or 3.7 raises candidates - 3.2 only happens after 3.1, and 3.8 happens wherever ads sit in the results. then 3.9 and 3.10 to make sure it is the right place. 3.11 where the trip starts somewhere other than here - mandatory on desktop, where both endpoints are typed fields.

questions.question: Which of these suggestions is your destination?
questions.why: The search bar suggests multiple places with similar names like Rochester, NY and Rochester Hills, so you must select the exact one to ensure accurate routing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the correct specific location was chosen from the autocomplete list rather than a similarly named but incorrect destination.
questions.check: Which suggestions does the list show, with their full names and regions?
questions.say_example: There's more than one. <Rochester, New York>, or <Rochester Hills, Michigan>. Which one is yours?

questions.question: Which past search should you reuse for your destination?
questions.why: Selecting a previously searched location from the 'TODAY' list, like the Queen Elizabeth Theatre, saves time over typing the full address manually.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the convenience of quickly selecting a familiar, recently searched location directly from your personal map history.
questions.check: Does the recent searches list show an entry matching the named destination?
questions.say_example: Reused today's search for <the Queen Elizabeth Theatre>.

questions.question: Which nearby restaurant do you want to select as your destination?
questions.why: The map displays multiple nearby restaurants with varying ratings, requiring a choice of which specific location to target.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally select a destination based on its specific map location and user ratings.
questions.check: Which places do the results list, with their names, ratings, and distances?
questions.say_example: Three restaurants close by. <Zabrero>, <4.5 stars>. <Enzo's>, <4.2>. Which one?

questions.question: Do the search results match what you asked for?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple restaurant pins like Zabrero and Enzo's Ristorante, requiring you to decide if your destination is among them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify if the displayed options match your specific intent before deciding to abandon the search.
questions.check: Do the listed result names and categories match what was searched for?
questions.say_example: These results don't look like your ask. You said <pharmacy>, these are <restaurants>. I'm searching again.

children.label: Drop a pin on the map

questions.question: Does the pin mark the entrance or parking lot, not just the middle of a big complex?
questions.why: Searching for a large area like an airport, hospital, or university often drops the pin in the center of the campus, which can lead the navigation to route you to a locked service road or the wrong side of the property.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually refine the pin placement to ensure the navigation guides you to the actual public entrance or parking garage.
questions.check: Does the place card show a street address, or only a coordinates-style label or bare plus code?
questions.say_example: The pin has no street address, just <a map point>. On a big property that can mean the middle of it, not the door.

children.label: Tell the ads from the results

questions.question: Is this the right place before you ask for directions?
questions.why: Reviewing the place card showing the rating, operating hours, and contact options ensures you have selected the correct Woolworths location before requesting directions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify the store's reviews, exact business hours, and other specific details to ensure it is the right location before traveling.
questions.check: What name, address, and hours does the place card show?
questions.say_example: Found <Woolworths> on <Main St>, open until <9>. I'm getting directions.

questions.question: Do you want to review the destination's details, such as hours, reviews, and popular times?
questions.why: The screen displayed comprehensive business information, including a review summary, popular times, and nearby public transport options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses out on contextual information about the destination, like how busy it is or its exact hours, which might influence their travel plans.
questions.check: What review summary, hours, and popular-times details does the card show?
questions.say_example: <Busiest around 5>. Reviews mention <parking being tight>.

questions.question: Is the destination marked as permanently or temporarily closed?
questions.why: The business's information card might display a red warning indicating it is closed, meaning routing there would result in a wasted trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to cancel or change your plans before driving to a location that is no longer open.
questions.check: Does the place card show 'Permanently closed' or 'Temporarily closed'?
questions.say_example: The page marks this place <permanently closed>. Going there wastes the trip. Want me to find another <branch>?

children.label: Preview the place in Street View

questions.question: Should you check the Street View to see what the area looks like?
questions.why: The screen shows a Street View thumbnail for the dropped pin, which lets you visually confirm the road and shops at the destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual context of the destination's surroundings, which helps in recognizing the exact spot upon arrival.
questions.check: Is a Street View thumbnail shown for the pin?
questions.say_example: Street View of the door exists if you want a look.

questions.question: Should you preview the street-level view of specific turns on your route?
questions.why: The step-by-step directions list includes camera icons that open a Street View pop-up to help you visualize the maneuver.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the chance to visually memorize confusing intersections or landmarks along the route yourself.
questions.check: Do steps in the directions list show camera icons that open Street View?
questions.say_example: The tricky turns have Street View previews.

questions.question: Which starting point should you select for the route?
questions.why: The screen displays a dropdown list of potential starting points, including 'Your location', saved places like 'Home', and recent searches, which determines where the directions will begin.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to calculate the route from their current physical location, their home address, or another specific starting point.
questions.check: What does the starting-point field show?
questions.say_example: Route starts from where you are now.

questions.question: Which suggestion is your starting point?
questions.why: The dropdown showed multiple cities named Harrington across different states and countries, requiring you to clarify your search to find the one in Washington.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct state is selected when multiple cities share the exact same name.
questions.check: Which start-point suggestions does the list show, with their regions?
questions.say_example: More than one <Harrington>. The list shows <Washington> and <Delaware>. Which is your start?

children.label: Shape the route
children.note: 4.1 opens the overview - on desktop it comes before 3 (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). then 4.2 to 4.6 in any order, each entered, read, and mostly put back: time pickers cancelled (FfFy), what-ifs reverted (bQbE), slower alternates chosen only to demonstrate switching (fnxA, obk4). 4.7 descends when transit wins the comparison time. 4.8 and 4.9 before any commit; 4.10 wherever a number crosses screens. every keeper reaches this goal, and eight end the task without ever starting guidance.

questions.question: Which ride-hailing service do you want to use for this trip?
questions.why: The ride service tab displays third-party providers like DiDi along with their current wait times, requiring you to choose a specific company to fulfill the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to select your preferred ride-hailing provider based on your existing accounts, brand trust, or the specific wait times shown.
questions.check: Which ride services does the tab list, with their wait times?
questions.say_example: The ride tab lists <DiDi>, about <13 minutes> out. Booking happens in their app, on your account. Which service?

questions.question: Before navigation starts from this place card, are the route options reviewed rather than letting the start button run straight through?
questions.why: The screen shows the destination's information card with options to get directions, start navigation immediately, save, or share the location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide whether they want to review different route options first or jump straight into active navigation.
questions.check: Which actions does the place card offer?
questions.say_example: Took <Directions> rather than instant <Start>.

questions.question: What are your starting and destination locations, and how are you traveling?
questions.why: The form requires entering a starting point in field A and a destination in field B, along with selecting a travel mode from the dropdown, to calculate the route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify your exact starting point, add intermediate stops, or ensure your preferred mode of transportation is selected.
questions.check: What do the start field, the destination field, and the mode selector show?
questions.say_example: Got it. From <where you are> to <the Queen Elizabeth Theatre>, driving.

questions.question: Should you select public transit to review the available routes and estimated travel times?
questions.why: The screen provides a travel mode dropdown menu, allowing you to switch to public transit to reveal specific departure schedules and trip durations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate whether taking public transit is the most efficient or convenient option for your specific schedule.
questions.check: What durations does the transit tab show?
questions.say_example: Transit runs <9 hours> and up.

questions.question: Should you check the rideshare tab to compare the estimated fare and wait time against public transit?
questions.why: Maps often integrate with apps like Uber or Lyft, showing estimated costs and pickup times as a distinct alternative to driving yourself or taking the bus.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to realize that hailing a ride might be more cost-effective or faster than waiting for a delayed transit line.
questions.check: Does a rideshare tab show fare estimates and pickup times?
questions.say_example: Rideshare estimate <$18>, pickup in <4 minutes>.

questions.question: Do you want to review the walking route and its estimated time?
questions.why: The screen displays a dotted line for the walking path and an ETA of 1 day and 17 hours, which helps you evaluate if walking is a practical choice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally assess the feasibility of the walking route and decide if the lengthy travel time is acceptable.
questions.check: Does the walking ETA show a duration in days?
questions.say_example: Walking this would take <1 day and 17 hours>. That's not a walk. Driving or transit instead?

questions.question: Do you want the mode the app picked, or another one?
questions.why: The map automatically selected a 9-minute car route, but shows alternative modes like transit, walking, and cycling that might be better suited for your trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to choose a different way to travel or engage with the fuel-saving settings if the agent automatically accepts the default driving route.
questions.check: Which mode is selected, and what time does each mode tab show?
questions.say_example: Driving, <9 minutes>. Transit shows <32>.

questions.question: Which route option should you choose?
questions.why: The screen displayed a fastest route taking 1 hour and 41 minutes alongside a longer alternative taking 1 hour and 46 minutes, requiring a comparison of time and distance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally weigh the trade-offs between travel time and distance to select the path you prefer.
questions.check: Which routes are listed, with their times and distances, and which one is selected?
questions.say_example: Taking the fastest route, <1 hour 41>. The next one is <5 minutes> slower.

questions.question: Do you want to choose the route that saves fuel, even if it might be slightly slower?
questions.why: The route card highlights a green leaf icon and states 'Saves 6% petrol' or 'Saves 6% more petrol than alternate routes'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to make an environmentally friendly or cost-saving choice if the agent strictly optimizes for the fastest time.
questions.check: Does a route card show a fuel-saving label such as 'Saves 6% petrol'?
questions.say_example: The picked route is the fuel-saver. <Saves 6% petrol>.

questions.question: Does the shape of the route on the map reveal a convoluted path through side streets?
questions.why: The map visually displays the route as a blue line, making it instantly obvious if a technically faster route actually involves a stressful, jagged path through residential areas rather than sticking to main roads.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to quickly visually assess the driving complexity of the route, potentially being directed by the agent onto a stressful, turn-heavy path just to save one minute.
questions.check: (image) Does the drawn route line wind through a street grid rather than staying on main roads?
questions.say_example: The fast route zigzags through side streets. The <2 minutes> it saves buys a lot of turns.

questions.question: Is the traffic delay concentrated in one specific bottleneck or spread out along the entire route?
questions.why: The map uses red and yellow color-coding along the route line to show exactly where traffic is bad, which a sighted user absorbs instantly at a glance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Without seeing the map, you lose the ability to mentally prepare for a sudden, stressful dead-stop versus a generally slow but moving drive.
questions.check: (image, partly text) Do delay chips or colored segments show where the slow stretch sits along the route line?
questions.say_example: The delay is one stretch on <I-5 north>. The rest runs clear.

questions.question: Does this route require driving over major bridges, through tunnels, or along winding mountain roads?
questions.why: The map's base layer visually reveals if the route line crosses water, goes underground, or snakes through tight topography.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual warning of geographic features that might trigger driving anxiety (like fear of heights) or require specific vehicle handling.
questions.check: Does any step in the directions list name a bridge, tunnel, or ferry?
questions.say_example: The route crosses <the Bay Bridge>.

children.label: Set the departure or arrival time

questions.question: When do you want to leave or arrive?
questions.why: The screen displays a time picker with tabs for 'Leave' and 'Arrive' along with date and time wheels, allowing you to check routes and traffic for future conditions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent chooses the time for you, you lose the ability to align the route estimates and transit schedules with your actual personal schedule.
questions.check: What does the time selector show — Leave now, or a set date and time?
questions.say_example: Leaving now. The picker can plan a later start if you ever want one.

questions.question: When do you need to leave to arrive by your target time?
questions.why: The screen showed different suggested departure times, such as 12:00 or 12:05, depending on which route you take to arrive by 1:00 PM.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to evaluate the different route options and choose your own departure time to build in a comfortable buffer.
questions.check: What departure times does the page list against the arrive-by time?
questions.say_example: To be there by <1:00>, leave by <12:05>.

questions.question: Should you search for the last available transit route of the day?
questions.why: The departure time menu offers an option to find the final transit run of the day, which is crucial for planning late-night travel before services shut down.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify exactly when transit services end for the night, risking being stranded if they stay out too late.
questions.check: Does the departure menu show a last-service option or a final departure time?
questions.say_example: The last <bus> tonight runs at <11:40>. Miss it and there's no ride back.

questions.question: Should you add any extra stops or waypoints to your route?
questions.why: The screen displays an 'Add Destination' link and a new input field, allowing you to build a multi-stop trip that recalculates the overall path and travel time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to spontaneously add or remove errands along the way based on how the initial route shapes up.
questions.check: Does the directions panel show an Add Destination option?
questions.say_example: No extra stops. You didn't ask for any.

questions.question: Which alternative path should you drag the route line to?
questions.why: Dragging the route line reveals tooltips with updated distances and estimated times for alternative paths, such as the 38-minute option via W Carmen Ave.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually customize your exact path based on personal preferences like driving closer to the coast.
questions.check: Does dragging the line show a tooltip with a new time and distance?
questions.say_example: Kept the suggested path. No dragging.

children.label: Pick the transit itinerary
children.note: 4.7.1, then 4.7.2 on the chosen option; 4.7.3 and 4.7.4 while reading it; 4.7.5 and 4.7.6 where the platform has them. no keeper boards anything.

questions.question: Which transit route should you choose based on the schedule and real-time status?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple transit options with their durations, line numbers, and real-time status indicators to help ensure a timely arrival.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the trade-offs between different transit lines, transfer times, and your own tolerance for potential delays.
questions.check: Which transit options are listed, with duration, line, and live status?
questions.say_example: Taking the <7:45> train, <46 minutes>. The page says <on time>.

questions.question: Are you okay with the fare cost for this transit route?
questions.why: The transit options list displays the fare (e.g., '$1.25') alongside the travel time, which is a factor in choosing between routes or modes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to factor the out-of-pocket cost of the transit ticket into their travel decision.
questions.check: What fare does the option list show?

questions.question: What are the exact steps, timings, and delays for this transit route?
questions.why: The detailed route view shows real-time bus delays, wait times, and provides a map preview of the walking segments between stops.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to visually verify the walking paths between transit stops and mentally prepare for specific wait times or delays.
questions.check: What legs, times, wait times, and delays does the detailed itinerary show?
questions.say_example: Bus <41> at <10:52> from <Riverside Dr>, then a <4 minute> walk.

questions.question: Is the scheduled transfer time between transit lines actually feasible for your walking speed?
questions.why: The transit itinerary might calculate a very tight 1- or 2-minute connection window between a bus and a train, leaving no margin for error if the first leg is slightly late or the platform is far.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to evaluate the risk of missing a tight connection and opting for a safer route with a larger time buffer.
questions.check: What transfer time does the itinerary show between the legs?
questions.say_example: The change at <Central> allows <2 minutes>. Only you know if that's enough walking time.

questions.question: Should you check the live location and status of the bus on this route?
questions.why: Tapping the moving bus icon reveals a tooltip with real-time updates like 'Early in 6 min', which helps confirm exactly when the transit will arrive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of seeing the exact live location and real-time schedule adjustments of their specific bus.
questions.check: Does the live status show the vehicle running early, late, or on time?
questions.say_example: Your <bus> is running <6 minutes early>. It won't wait.

questions.question: Is there a visual icon indicating that this specific transit vehicle is currently crowded?
questions.why: Transit options often feature small visual badges (like little person icons) that indicate live crowdedness based on user reports or historical data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual cue about current passenger volume, missing the opportunity to choose a slightly slower but much less crowded and more comfortable transit line.
questions.check: Does the option show a crowdedness label or badge text?
questions.say_example: The <10:52> is marked <usually full>.

questions.question: Do you want to view the exact walking path for this transit segment on the map?
questions.why: The screen displayed detailed transit steps with a 'MAP' button next to the walking segment, letting you visualize exactly where to walk to catch your ride.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually familiarize yourself with the exact walking path to the transit stop before you start moving.
questions.check: Does the walking segment offer a map view of the path?
questions.say_example: The walk to the stop is mapped. It's in the report.

questions.question: Do you want to restrict the search to specific types of public transit?
questions.why: The route options screen displays a 'Preferred Modes' section with toggles for bus, train, subway, and tram to customize the transit results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a route using a transit mode you prefer to avoid, rather than tailoring the journey to your comfort.
questions.check: Which transit modes do the Preferred Modes toggles show switched on?
questions.say_example: All transit types left on.

questions.question: Do you want to prioritize fewer transfers or less walking for this trip?
questions.why: The screen shows options for 'Best route', 'Fewer transfers', and 'Less walking', which significantly alter the suggested transit itinerary based on your physical needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just select the default best route, missing your personal need to minimize physical exertion or complex connections.
questions.check: Which option is selected among Best route, Fewer transfers, and Less walking?
questions.say_example: Kept <Best route>. <Less walking> exists if standing and walking are the harder part.

questions.question: Which scheduled departure time and route combination should you choose?
questions.why: The schedule explorer shows that shifting your departure time by just a few minutes can significantly change your total travel time and transit lines.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance your preferred departure time against the convenience and speed of the resulting transit options.
questions.check: What total travel times does the timetable show for nearby departure times?
questions.say_example: Leaving <10 minutes> later cuts it to <48 minutes> from <1 hour 15>.

questions.question: Should you check the alternative departure times for the bus in case you miss the currently delayed one?
questions.why: The narrator notes that the detailed transit view shows what other times the bus will pass, which is crucial backup information if you miss a delayed connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of knowing exactly when the next bus arrives if you happen to miss the one you are scheduled to catch.
questions.check: What later departure times does the detailed view list for the same line?
questions.say_example: If you miss it, the next <41> runs at <11:12>.

questions.question: Where exactly are the toll roads on this route?
questions.why: The step-by-step directions list marks toll roads with an asterisk, letting you tap to preview the specific locations where you will be charged.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually verify the exact locations of the toll roads on the map before driving.
questions.check: Which steps in the directions list carry toll markers?
questions.say_example: Tolls sit on <the E-470 stretch>.

questions.question: Do you want to review the step-by-step directions for this route before starting navigation?
questions.why: The screen displays a 1 hour 41 minute ETA for the fastest route, and opening the steps allows you to preview the exact roads and turns you will be taking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to mentally prepare for the drive or verify that the specific path avoids undesirable roads and complex intersections.
questions.check: What roads and turns does the step list show?
questions.say_example: The route runs <I-76 west>, then <CO-52>.

questions.question: Are you okay proceeding without knowing the exact toll amounts?
questions.why: The map indicates the route includes tolls but does not display the exact cost upfront.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to accept unknown toll costs or look for a toll-free alternative.
questions.check: Does the route show a toll warning without a toll amount?
questions.say_example: This route has tolls, and the page doesn't say how much. Bring a way to pay.

questions.question: Does the route overview show any warning?
questions.why: The route overview displays critical alerts like 'Route may be affected by Coastal Flood Warning' or 'Route crosses a country border', which could mean delays, danger, or needing a passport.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the heads-up to prepare for hazardous driving conditions or to ensure they have the necessary travel documents before setting off.
questions.check: Does the route overview show any warning text — weather, border crossing, closures, restricted or private roads, limited parking, or steep and sidewalk-free stretches?
questions.say_example: One warning on this route: <it crosses a country border>. That can mean <a passport check>.

questions.question: Does the distance shown in the search results match the distance in the location details?
questions.why: The search result lists the distance to Audi Victoria as 8.5 km, but the location details pop-up contradicts this by displaying 15 km.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses trust in the map's accuracy and might misjudge their travel time if the agent proceeds with conflicting distance data.
questions.check: Does the distance in the search result equal the distance on the place details view?
questions.say_example: One screen says <8.5 km>, another says <15>. I'm trusting the route screen and noting the clash.

questions.question: Does the time on the transit tab match the route it opens?
questions.why: The transit tab icon displays an estimated travel time of 6 hours and 24 minutes, but the recommended route in the detailed list actually takes 9 hours and 5 minutes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate scheduling expectations if the agent blindly trusts the tab's initial estimate instead of checking the actual route details.
questions.check: Does the time on the transit tab equal the recommended route's time in the detailed list?
questions.say_example: The tab promises <6 hours 24>. The route it opens takes <9 hours 5>. Count on the longer one.

questions.question: Do the individual segment times add up to the total estimated trip time?
questions.why: Checking that the 4-minute walk, 19-minute bus ride, and 5-minute walk correctly sum to the 28-minute total ensures the route's time estimate is reliable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to manually verify the math behind the transit estimate to ensure there are no hidden delays or calculation errors.
questions.check: Do the leg times shown sum to the stated total?
questions.say_example: The legs add to <28 minutes>, the total says <25>. One of those is wrong.

questions.question: Does the summarized travel time match the detailed time window?
questions.why: This matters because the screen displays conflicting numbers, such as a 37-minute summary alongside a 39-minute time window and a 37-mile distance label.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: A person delegating to an agent loses the ability to catch interface glitches or mislabeled units that could lead to inaccurate travel expectations.
questions.check: Does the summary time equal the time window shown on the detail view?
questions.say_example: The summary says <37 minutes>, the window says <39>. Plan on <39>.

questions.question: Does the route duration in the summary match the time shown on the traffic graph?
questions.why: The steps list summary displayed an 8 hr 34 min duration while the traffic graph showed 8 hr 49 min, creating uncertainty about the true estimated travel time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might report the shorter summary time without noticing the conflicting traffic graph, leaving you unprepared for a potentially longer trip.
questions.check: Does the summary duration equal the duration on the traffic graph?
questions.say_example: The list says <8 hours 34>, the graph says <8 hours 49>. I'd count on the longer one.

questions.question: Do the transit countdowns and departure times logically align with the current time?
questions.why: The screen displays conflicting information between the system clock, the scheduled departure time, and the live countdown, which makes it difficult to know exactly when the transit arrives.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly trust one of the conflicting time estimates without realizing the math does not add up, leading to a missed departure.
questions.check: Do the live countdown, the scheduled departure time, and the shown clock agree with each other?
questions.say_example: The countdown and the schedule disagree about the <bus>. Going by the schedule, <10:52>.

questions.question: Does the same street route show a different distance for walking than for driving?
questions.why: The screen shows the route via W Hargett St as 0.4 miles for walking but 0.5 miles for driving, indicating slight path differences between modes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might overlook this discrepancy and fail to realize that walking offers a slightly shorter physical path than driving.
questions.check: Do the walking and driving distances differ for the same named street route?
questions.say_example: Walking shows <0.4 miles>, driving <0.5>. One-way streets do that.

questions.question: Will the destination still be open by the time you arrive?
questions.why: The route overview shows an ETA (e.g., 2 hr 39 min), and the destination details indicate it closes at a specific time (e.g., 18:00), requiring a mental check to ensure the trip is not wasted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might arrive to find the business closed because the agent didn't cross-reference the estimated arrival time with the operating hours.
questions.check: What arrival time does the ETA give, and what closing time does the place card show?
questions.say_example: You'd get there around <6:40>. It closes at <6>.

questions.question: Do the time and distance estimates remain consistent after you start navigation?
questions.why: The route overview showed a 14-minute, 7.1 km trip, but the active navigation immediately dropped to 12 minutes and 6.6 km.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might fail to notice that the navigation app silently recalculated or altered the route upon starting.
questions.check: Do the time and distance after starting match the overview shown before starting?
questions.say_example: ETA moved from <14> to <12 minutes> once we started.

children.label: Run the navigation
children.note: 5.1, answering 5.2's prompt stack where it fires. 5.3 almost immediately - it is the most-touched in-drive control in the corpus. then 5.4 to 5.9 in any order as the drive demands. 5.10 is reached only in one spliced session. 5.11 ends it - every keeper who starts guidance and keeps recording stops it on purpose, except mo0Q, whose video simply ends mid-drive.

questions.question: Which side of the street is the destination on, or is it located inside a larger complex?
questions.why: The map visually places the destination pin on the left or right side of the road line, or deep inside a shaded area like a mall or airport.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial cue of exactly where to look or which lane to pull into as you approach the final destination.
questions.check: Does the final step in the directions say which side the destination is on?
questions.say_example: It'll be on your <right>.

questions.question: Ready to start — does the route read back right?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify the route's ETA, traffic conditions, and alternate paths before committing to the journey.
questions.check: What route, duration, and arrival time does the screen show at the START button?

questions.question: Does the selected route reflect my toll and highway preferences before I start navigation?
questions.why: The screen displays an 'Avoiding highways and tolls' banner alongside multiple route times, requiring you to confirm the updated route is acceptable before hitting start.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your specific route restrictions were successfully applied before beginning the drive.
questions.check: Does the route banner state it is avoiding the things that were asked for — tolls, highways, ferries?
questions.say_example: You asked for no tolls, but the route doesn't say it's avoiding them. I'm fixing that before we start.

questions.question: Do you want to navigate directly to the destination or route to a parking lot first?
questions.why: The screen suggests a nearby parking lot and offers to view more lots before you hit GO.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the convenience of having the map guide you directly to an available parking space instead of just the general address.
questions.check: Does the screen offer a parking lot before the destination, with a view-more-lots option?
questions.say_example: There's parking <2 minutes> before the destination. Straight there, or park first?

questions.question: Did you confirm that active turn-by-turn navigation has started?
questions.why: Seeing the active navigation panel with the ETA, duration, and distance confirms the app is ready to guide you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the app successfully transitioned from route planning to active, real-time guidance.
questions.check: Does the screen show the active navigation panel with a live ETA, duration, and distance?
questions.say_example: Navigation confirmed running.

questions.question: Should you add the vignette or just drive without it?
questions.why: The screen showed a ticket alert warning that the route requires a vignette, requiring a choice between adding the pass or bypassing the warning.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically skips the vignette warning, you might drive on a toll road without the proper pass and receive a fine.
questions.check: Does the screen show an alert that the route requires a vignette or toll pass, and does it say one is missing?
questions.say_example: This route needs a <vignette>, a road pass, and the app says there isn't one. Driving without it risks a fine. Add it, or reroute?

questions.question: How should I respond to the notification and data sharing prompts to start navigation?
questions.why: The app displays a series of pop-ups regarding notifications and data sharing that must be dismissed or accepted to access the active turn-by-turn navigation screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their privacy preferences regarding app notifications and navigation data sharing.
questions.check: Which pop-ups block the navigation screen, and what does each ask for?
questions.say_example: Dismissed the notification and data-sharing pop-ups with no.

questions.question: Does starting navigation silence your calls and notifications?
questions.why: The screen displays an alert indicating that notifications are silenced when navigation starts and restored when it ends, confirming that a driving focus mode is active.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that starting the navigation app automatically alters their device's system-wide notification settings.
questions.check: Does the screen say notifications are silenced during navigation and restored after?
questions.say_example: Your calls and alerts go quiet while navigating. They come back when it ends.

questions.question: Do you want to allow Google Maps to access your motion and fitness activity?
questions.why: The prompt states the app uses this data to show saved parking information and public transport trip progress, which requires sharing personal physical activity data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to share your personal motion and fitness data with the app.
questions.check: Does the prompt ask for motion and fitness access, and what does it say the data is used for?
questions.say_example: Said no to motion and fitness access.

questions.question: The blocking safety warning states the driving responsibilities being accepted - do you read and accept it yourself?
questions.why: The app displays a safety warning pop-up that blocks the active navigation screen until you tap 'OK'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally read and acknowledge the legal and safety responsibilities of driving.
questions.check: Does a safety warning pop-up block the navigation screen until OK is tapped?
questions.say_example: Cleared the safety notice.

questions.question: Do you want to inspect the route ahead for traffic and then re-center the map?
questions.why: Panning the map reveals a red section on highway '34' indicating traffic, and the 'Re-centre' button quickly snaps the view back to your current location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial awareness of exactly where the traffic delays are located along your journey.
questions.check: Do delay chips or colored stretches appear on the route ahead?
questions.say_example: Red stretch on <highway 34> ahead. The ETA already counts it.

questions.question: Are you monitoring the active navigation and current trip estimates?
questions.why: Confirming the active navigation screen with live updates like the 1 hr 32 min duration and 41 km distance ensures the route is successfully underway.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses real-time awareness of their exact travel time, distance, and immediate turn-by-turn instructions.
questions.check: What live duration and distance does the navigation panel show?
questions.say_example: <1 hour 32> to go, <41 km>.

questions.question: Do you want to review the entire route and alternative paths before re-centering?
questions.why: Checking the overview map allows you to evaluate the full 87-mile path and the alternative route labeled 'Similar ETA' before returning to active navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually inspect the entire route and decide if the alternative path better suits your driving preferences.
questions.check: Does the overview show an alternative route and its ETA label?
questions.say_example: An alternative shows <similar ETA>. Staying put.

questions.question: After adding the stop, is your original destination still the end of the route?
questions.why: The screen shows buttons for 'New drive' and 'Add a stop', requiring a choice between replacing the existing itinerary or creating a multi-stop journey.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify whether they want to abandon their original destination or just make a detour along the way.

questions.question: Which specific location do you want to add as a stop along your route?
questions.why: Typing 'birming' into the search bar brings up multiple distinct suggestions like 'Birmingham Airport' and 'Birmingham New Street', requiring you to select the exact destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the precise point of interest or station you want to visit during your trip.
questions.check: Which suggestions does the stop search list show?
questions.say_example: Two matches. <Birmingham Airport>, or <Birmingham New Street>. Which stop is yours?

questions.question: Which gas station do you want to add as a stop?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple gas station options with varying ratings and detour times, such as a Tesco with a 12-minute detour versus a bp with a 6-minute detour.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the trade-off between a shorter detour time and a higher-rated or preferred brand of gas station.
questions.check: Which stations are listed, with their detour times?

questions.question: Do you want to search for any stops like gas stations or restaurants along your route?
questions.why: The screen displays quick-search categories like 'Gas stations' and 'Restaurants' alongside recent searches, offering an easy way to add a convenient stop to your trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to spontaneously decide if you need to pick up groceries or coffee based on your immediate personal needs.
questions.check: Does the search screen offer stop categories along the route?

questions.question: Which type of incident do you want to report on the map?
questions.why: The screen displays a menu of reportable incidents like crashes, speed cameras, and congestion to warn other drivers on the route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to accurately report the specific real-world hazard you are currently seeing on the road.

questions.check: Which detail options does the report screen offer?

questions.question: Do you want to authorize Waze to access your Spotify account?

questions.check: Does the screen show arrival options at the stop, including a continue choice?

questions.question: Do you want to stop the automatic navigation?

questions.question: Do you want to review the step-by-step distances on the printable directions page?

questions.question: Do you want to use the storage this offline map needs?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking to confirm the download of the selected map area, noting it will use up to 80 MB of free space.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might approve the download without knowing if you have enough device storage or cellular data to spare.
questions.check: What size does the download prompt state?
questions.say_example: Downloading the offline map. About <80 MB>.

questions.question: Are you okay with the downloaded offline map taking up more storage space than initially estimated?
questions.why: The screen initially estimated the offline map would use up to 80 MB, but later showed the downloaded file taking up 108 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor their device storage accurately when the agent fails to notice that a download exceeded its estimated size.
questions.check: Does the downloaded size shown match the size the prompt promised?
questions.say_example: The map took <108 MB>. The prompt said <80>.

questions.question: Do you want to update the downloaded map before it expires?
questions.why: The screen indicates that the downloaded map will expire on June 5, 2023, unless it is updated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use your device's data and storage to keep this specific offline map current.
questions.check: Does the offline map list show an expiry date?
questions.say_example: Your offline map expires <June 5>. After that it stops working unless it updates.

questions.question: Should you delete any existing offline maps to free up space?
questions.why: The screen displays a previously downloaded 49 MB map, and removing it can free up device storage before saving a new area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your device's storage management and the choice of which old maps to keep or discard.
questions.check: What sizes do the existing downloaded maps show?
questions.say_example: Left the old <49 MB> map alone.

questions.question: Should you update the expiring offline map using your mobile data?
questions.why: The app warns that downloading the map update over a mobile network could result in extra data charges.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to weigh the urgency of the map update against potential mobile data fees.
questions.check: Does the app warn that the update will use the mobile network and may incur charges?
questions.say_example: Updating now uses mobile data, and that can cost. Wait for Wi-Fi?

questions.question: Should you restrict the app to only use Wi-Fi or downloaded offline maps?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Wi-Fi only' toggle and a toast message explaining that without a Wi-Fi network, only offline maps will function.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose whether to restrict data usage via the app's built-in toggle or through the device's system settings.
questions.check: Is the Wi-Fi only toggle on, and what does the notice say happens without Wi-Fi?
questions.say_example: Wi-Fi-only stays on. Off Wi-Fi you'd have only the downloaded maps.

questions.question: With Wi-Fi and mobile data switched off, does the downloaded map actually produce a route, or does routing fail?
questions.why: The Android quick settings panel displays active network connections like Wi-Fi that must be toggled off to ensure the app relies solely on downloaded data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the map will successfully provide directions without an active internet connection.
questions.check: Does the quick settings panel show which network connections are on?
questions.say_example: Turning off Wi-Fi to test the offline map. I'll put it back after.

questions.question: Is the destination now on screen the one you asked to route to, or did a failed route leave a different search in the box?
questions.why: The audio claims to route to a gas station, but the screen shows a failed route to High Falls followed by a new search for Genesee Brew House.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate destination tracking if the agent relies on the spoken intent rather than noticing the actual on-screen routing failures and changes.
questions.check: Does the destination named on the screen match the destination that was spoken aloud?
questions.say_example: I said <the gas station>, but the screen is routing to <High Falls>. I'm fixing that before we move.

questions.question: Do you want this offline route without live traffic?
questions.why: The screen displays an offline icon and 'No traffic data', meaning the 15-minute estimate cannot account for current road conditions or delays.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to find an internet connection for live traffic updates or to delay the trip until real-time data is available.
questions.check: Does the screen show an offline icon or a no-traffic-data notice?
questions.say_example: You're offline, so no traffic data. The <15 minute> estimate can't see jams or closures.

questions.question: What starting point should the offline route begin from?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'No routes found in your offline maps' error, requiring you to choose a new origin within the downloaded area to successfully calculate a route.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to troubleshoot offline map limitations by manually selecting an alternative starting point.
questions.check: Does the screen show a no-routes-found-in-your-offline-maps error?
questions.say_example: No offline route from where you are. I can only start it from inside the downloaded area, and then the first directions won't match where you stand. Where should it begin?

children.label: Share your live location
children.note: 8.1, then 8.2 to 8.4 in the sheet's order; 8.5 fires mid-flow when the platform demands background access; 8.6 closes the loop. QULM runs all of it; aGGT opens the sheet and backs out.

questions.question: Do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The app offers to share your continuous location with others across Google services, which updates even when the app is not in use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide whether your continuous, real-time whereabouts are broadcasted to others.
questions.check: Does the screen describe sharing continuous location across services, updating even when the app is not in use?
questions.say_example: Opened location sharing, as you asked. It keeps updating even with the app closed.

questions.question: How long do you want to share your real-time location?
questions.why: The screen provides options to share your location for a set time, such as one hour, or indefinitely until turned off, which directly affects your privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strictly control the duration of your location sharing, potentially exposing your whereabouts longer than intended.
questions.check: Which duration options does the sharing screen offer?
questions.say_example: How long should they see where you are? <An hour>, or until you turn it off?

questions.question: Which app do you want to use to share the location link?
questions.why: The screen shows a sharing menu with multiple communication apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Messages to choose from.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide which specific messaging platform is used to send your location to others.
questions.check: Which apps does the share sheet list?
questions.say_example: Shared through <WhatsApp>, like you said.

questions.question: Who should receive your live location link?
questions.why: The WhatsApp 'Select contacts' screen requires you to choose a recipient from your recent chats to send the live location link to.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to safely select your own number to test the feature without broadcasting your location to other contacts.
questions.check: Which contacts does the selection screen list?
questions.say_example: Who gets the link? They'll see where you are the whole time.

questions.question: Do you accept that anyone holding the link can see your name, photo, and live location?
questions.why: The app explicitly warns that anyone with the generated link will be able to see your personal details and live location, requiring you to accept this privacy risk to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the privacy implications of broadcasting your live location and to decide whether to keep future warnings enabled.
questions.check: Does the warning state that anyone with the link can see the name, photo, and real-time location, and is a don't-show-again option present?
questions.say_example: Anyone holding this link can see your name, photo, and where you are, live. Still send it?
